text: I want to see the city before it begins demanding things from me.
context: A note to myself after an early walk.

text: A city is edited every day by the people who fix, paint, plant and sell at its edges.
context: Saved for the idea, not the author.

text: I have twenty-six photos of hand-painted shop signs and none of them have names.
A good desk makes it easier to begin, not harder to leave.
context: A line from a Sunday reset.

text: The best field guide tells you what to notice, not what to think.
There is a tiny patch of basil growing in a crack beside the bus stop.
Could I make a guide to the places that make a neighbourhood feel looked after?
A handwritten price board is a small public promise.
context: A saved line about ordinary design.

text: Remember the woman who waters the planters outside the closed cinema.
Maybe my camera roll is a map of the things I do not want the city to lose.
Small acts of maintenance are a kind of local authorship.
What if a map could show who keeps a place alive instead of only where it is?
context: A question recorded on a walk.
